chunks: And among what Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā narrated, from al-Sindī ibn al-Rabīʿ, from al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥajjāj, from Abī Ibrāhīm عليه السلام, who said:
Concerning a man who does not know whether he has prayed one rakʿah or two, he said: He builds upon one rakʿah.

key_terms.الرَّجُلِ: the man being asked about in the legal case
key_terms.الرَّكْعَةِ: the one rakʿah taken as the basis

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if he doubts whether he has prayed one rakʿah or two?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding doubt in the number of rakʿahs in salat (prayer), specifically when one is unsure whether he has prayed one or two. The ruling is to proceed on the basis of the lesser number, counting it as one rakʿah.
